events.did: Worked at the laptop with the black coding window and the same two words glowing white on the screen
events.quote_anchor: a plate of pie crumbs—apple this time—at his elbow and the laptop filled by the black coding window, the same two words glowing white on the screen.

events.did: Cracked his knuckles and checked his watch, making a final attempt at the code when he saw Jenny coming
events.quote_anchor: He cracked his knuckles, and checked his watch, was about to make a final attempt when he caught sight of Jenny coming toward the booth.

events.did: Double-clicked to collapse the coding window before Jenny glanced at the gardening forum page on his screen
events.quote_anchor: He double-clicked and the coding window collapsed, right before she glanced over his shoulder at the gardening forum page.

events.did: Told Mitch that a guy came into the diner a few days back looking for him
events.quote_anchor: “Oh, hey. I almost forgot. A guy came in a few days back, looking for you.”

events.did: Said the man did not seem to mind and would swing by Mitch's place next time he passed through
events.quote_anchor: Said he’d just swing by your place, next time he was passing through.

events.did: Felt the blood drain from his face into the bottom of his shoes
events.quote_anchor: Mitch felt the blood drain from his face, pool in the bottom of his shoes.

events.did: Said the man never gave his name
events.quote_anchor: The waitress frowned. “Come to think of it, he didn’t say.”

events.did: Drew cash from his wallet, left the booth and tipped his head to Jenny while his mind sprinted toward the truck and the cabin
events.quote_anchor: But as his hand drew the cash from his wallet, as his legs shifted him out of the booth, as he tipped his head to Jenny

relations.did: Is the waitress at Herald Diner who teased Mitch about working hard and told him a man was looking for him
relations.quote_anchor: “Working hard or hardly working?” she said. “I’m guessing the first, based on the way you’re scowling at that screen.”

relations.did: Knew where Mitch lived, which made Jenny assume he was a friend
relations.quote_anchor: “I figured he was a friend, given that he knew where you lived.”

relations.did: Raced toward the truck and the cabin at the edge of the woods, thinking of Syd
relations.quote_anchor: his mind was in a full-out sprint, racing to the truck, pealing down the road toward the cabin at the edge of the woods.
